The test uses a single non-boundary string value. It does not exercise empty strings, null, very long strings, zero/negative numeric boundaries, or other edge inputs relevant to the key/value domain.
practices_evaluation.original_code:
// When: insert an entry using a special string key
  tabelaHash0.insere("[g1U^5", "[g1U^5");

practices_evaluation.justification: The test is short and self-contained with a clear Given-When-Then structure and no repeated setup across multiple tests. There is no evident duplication within the single test method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is short (<20 lines), linear, and does not include loops or complex conditionals. It follows a simple Arrange-Act-Assert pattern.

The test performs multiple meaningful assertions: it checks that pesquisa returns the expected value and that recuperaItens contains the inserted value, providing broader verification than a single superficial assertion.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out test methods are present. The test is active and runnable (@Test present).
The class-level Javadoc includes 'Requirement traceability: REQ-1001', which directly links the tests to a requirement ID.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a standard unit test exercising functional behavior. No performance or security testing is expected here; the method does not include timing/security assertions. Per decision rules, this practice is typically not applicable for unit tests.

The test method name is generic ('test7') and does not describe the scenario or expected result. Although the body includes Given-When-Then comments, the method name fails the descriptive naming convention.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class uses EvoSuite/EvoRunner (RunWith EvoRunner and EvoRunnerParameters) and the test method name 'test7' is consistent with auto-generated tests. These are signals of heavy code generation rather than focused handcrafted tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains Given-When-Then comments and descriptive assertions, indicating design intent and some BDD-style structuring, which suggests thoughtful design of this test case.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts with the public API of TabelaHash (insere, pesquisa, recuperaItens, imprime) and does not access private fields or use reflection, thus focusing on observable behavior.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals, assertTrue) and include descriptive failure messages for the main assertions, which aids diagnosis of failures.
The test includes concise Given-When-Then comments and a helpful class-level Javadoc; comments explain intent rather than restating obvious code, so they are appropriate and not excessive.
The test contains no calls to random, current time, Thread.sleep, or external services. Test uses local objects only, so it should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test operates on in-memory structures and local variables only; there are no file, DB, or static state modifications in the method that would persist between tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing meaningful categorization for selective execution.
